package_info.package_versions: Malicious version found on compromised mirror (exact version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The HandBrake application distributed via a compromised download mirror was trojanized to include a new variant of the Proton malware. This malware provides remote access, credential theft (including macOS keychain data), and persistence mechanisms, allowing attackers to fully compromise affected systems. The legitimate HandBrake app was replaced with this malicious version, leading unsuspecting users to install malware instead of the intended video transcoder.

execution_context.trigger: on application launch (runtime, immediately after user opens the app)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the HandBrake app bundle, typically within the main executable or a maliciously added supporting binary (e.g., /Applications/HandBrake.app/Contents/MacOS/HandBrake or a hidden binary within the app bundle)
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write access to user files and system locations)
environment_vars (access to user and system environment variables)
keychain_access (read access to macOS keychain for credential theft)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Proton malware variant (exact code not shown in report, but known behaviors include: establishing persistence via launch agents, collecting user credentials from the macOS keychain, capturing system information, and exfiltrating data to a remote command and control server. The malware may also execute remote commands and log keystrokes.)
malicious_snippets.code_language: Objective-C (compiled macOS binary, with possible embedded shell scripts for persistence and data exfiltration)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On application launch, the code establishes persistence by installing a launch agent, collects user credentials and system information (including keychain data), and sends this data via HTTPS POST to a remote command and control server, enabling credential exfiltration and remote attacker access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs credential theft by accessing the macOS keychain, establishes persistence using launch agents, and communicates with external command and control servers—all behaviors that are highly atypical and suspicious for a video transcoding application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate HandBrake app should only perform video transcoding and related file operations. It should not access sensitive credentials, install persistence mechanisms, or initiate outbound network connections unrelated to update checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise remote management tools may access credentials and establish persistence, but such behavior is never expected in consumer video transcoding software like HandBrake.
key_indicators: Access to macOS keychain for credential theft
Creation or modification of launch agents for persistence (e.g., ~/Library/LaunchAgents/fr.handbrake.activity_agent.plist)
Outbound HTTPS connections to Proton C2 infrastructure from the HandBrake process
Presence of hidden or unsigned binaries within the HandBrake app bundle
Execution of remote commands or keylogging activity

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized HandBrake app from the compromised mirror, replacing or adding the malicious app bundle to their system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code embedded within the app bundle

attack_chain.action: Upon launch, the Proton malware variant executes, establishing persistence via a launch agent and collecting sensitive data including credentials from the macOS keychain and system information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of credentials and system data, and enabling remote access

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials and system information are transmitted to the attacker's command and control server via outbound HTTPS requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access and control over the victim's system, with the ability to steal additional data or execute further commands

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections initiated by the HandBrake process, especially to unrecognized domains or IPs
Access to macOS keychain or credential stores by the HandBrake application or its child processes
Creation or modification of launch agents (e.g., files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/) by the HandBrake app
Presence of hidden or unsigned binaries within the HandBrake app bundle
file_indicators: HandBrake app bundle with modified or unsigned main executable
Presence of Proton malware components such as hidden binaries (e.g., /Applications/HandBrake.app/Contents/Resources/activity_agent.app or similar)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from the HandBrake process to known Proton C2 domains or IP addresses (as listed in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual network activity from HandBrake, such as connections to non-update-related servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for video transcoder applications like HandBrake making unexpected outbound network connections, especially HTTPS POST requests to known Proton C2 infrastructure. Detect access to the macOS keychain or creation of launch agents by non-administrative or non-security software. Verify app bundle signatures and compare hashes against known-good versions. Scan for the presence of hidden or unsigned binaries and specific launch agent files associated with Proton malware. Alert on any credential exfiltration attempts or remote command and control activity originating from the HandBrake process.
